oauthNotes: OAuth 2.0 (v2). Apps are created at api.slack.com/apps and are installed per workspace.

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Slack, so development can start without registering your own. A custom OAuth app is needed for your own branding on the consent screen, dedicated quota, or scopes beyond Composio's defaults. An agent that reads channel history for customers also needs its own Marketplace-approved app to avoid the reduced rate limits.

summary: A Slack app can be created and distributed to other workspaces without review. An agent that reads message history is a different case: outside the Slack Marketplace, the history methods are limited to one request per minute, so Marketplace approval becomes part of reaching production.

verdict.headline: Testing is available within minutes. An agent that reads message history for customers requires Slack Marketplace approval, which takes up to 12 weeks after 10 active workspaces have installed the app.
verdict.biggestRisk: Without Marketplace approval, conversations.history and conversations.replies are limited to 1 request per minute and 15 messages per request, which makes history-reading agents impractical.

paths.name: Marketplace-listed app for customer workspaces
paths.whenThisApplies: The app is sold or distributed commercially and reads channel or thread history. This is the usual case for an AI agent.

timeToFirstLogin.basis: Create the app from a manifest and install it to a development workspace.

activeEffort.basis: Estimate. Listing content, demo video, test credentials and review responses. No direct source.

waitTime.basis: Slack: preliminary review up to 10 business days, then functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions.

timeToProduction.basis: Review time plus the time needed to reach 10 active workspaces, which Slack requires before submission.

steps.title: Generate the app manifest
steps.detail: The agent drafts a manifest with the redirect URL and the minimum bot scopes. See Prepared materials.

steps.title: Create the app from the manifest
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps, choose to create an app from a manifest, paste it, and select a development workspace.

steps.title: Install to the development workspace and test
steps.detail: Install the app, copy the client ID and secret into Composio, and run a test connection.
gotchas: Decide on token rotation before launch. It cannot be turned off once enabled.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Complete Slack's distribution checklist. All OAuth redirect URLs must use SSL.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Slack accepts a Marketplace submission only after the app is installed on 10 or more workspaces used in the past 28 days.
gotchas: During this period the reduced history rate limits apply to every new installation.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace submission
steps.detail: The agent drafts the listing text, scope justifications and demo video script. Provide test credentials for your service.

steps.title: Submit the app for review
steps.detail: Submit from the app settings page. Feedback is returned within the submission flow.

steps.title: Slack reviews the app
steps.detail: A preliminary review is followed by a functional review.

estTime.basis: Slack: up to 10 business days, then up to 10 weeks.

steps.title: Publish the listing
steps.detail: Publish from the app settings page once approved.
gotchas: The published configuration is locked. Changing scopes or features requires resubmission, with up to 6 weeks of review.

paths.name: Distributed app without a Marketplace listing
paths.whenThisApplies: The app is installed by other workspaces but does not depend on reading message history, for example it only posts messages.

timeToFirstLogin.basis: Same setup as the Marketplace path.

waitTime.basis: No provider review on this path.

timeToProduction.basis: Public distribution is activated by the developer without review.

steps.title: Create the app from a manifest
steps.detail: Same as steps 1 to 3 of the Marketplace path.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Complete the distribution checklist. Other workspaces can then install the app through OAuth.
gotchas: Slack states that apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted to the Marketplace.
History methods are limited to 1 request per minute on this path.

paths.name: Internal app for your own workspace
paths.whenThisApplies: Only your own organisation uses the app.

waitTime.basis: No provider review on this path.

timeToProduction.basis: A new app can be installed in its own workspace immediately.

steps.title: Create and install the app
steps.detail: Create the app from a manifest and install it to your workspace. Internal customer-built apps are not affected by the reduced rate limits.

requirements.detail: Installed and used within the past 28 days, before a Marketplace submission is accepted.
Required for new submissions and for updates that add functionality or scopes.
Reviewers need credentials to access your service.
Required before public distribution can be activated.
Slack expects listed apps to be maintained and supported.

nuances.title: History methods are limited to 1 request per minute outside the Marketplace
nuances.detail: For commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace, conversations.history and conversations.replies moved from Tier 3 to Tier 1, with a maximum of 15 messages per request. Marketplace apps and internal apps are exempt.

nuances.title: Marketplace submission requires 10 active workspaces first
nuances.detail: The app must be distributed unlisted, under the reduced limits, until it reaches the threshold.

nuances.title: Token rotation is irreversible
nuances.detail: Without rotation, access tokens never expire. With rotation, they expire every 12 hours and refresh tokens are single use. Rotation cannot be turned off once enabled.

nuances.title: A published listing is locked
nuances.detail: Scopes, features and configuration cannot change without resubmission. Reviews of changes take up to 6 weeks.

nuances.title: Existing installations kept their previous limits
nuances.detail: The May 2025 changelog states that the reduced limits do not affect existing installations. Later reports describe a March 2026 cut-off for those installations, which this research did not confirm against Slack's documentation.

blockers.cause: The app is commercially distributed and not Marketplace-approved, so the method is limited to 1 request per minute.
blockers.fix: Submit the app to the Marketplace. Until approval, cache results and request at most 15 messages per call.

blockers.cause: The app has fewer than 10 active workspaces.
blockers.fix: Activate public distribution and onboard workspaces until 10 have used the app within 28 days.

blockers.symptom: Other workspaces cannot install the app
blockers.cause: Public distribution is not activated. New apps install only in their own workspace.
blockers.fix: Complete the distribution checklist in the app settings.

handoffKit.title: App manifest (YAML)
handoffKit.content:
display_information:
  name: <Your product name>
  description: <One-line description>
features:
  bot_user:
    display_name: <Your product name>
    always_online: false
oauth_config:
  redirect_urls:
    - https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
  scopes:
    bot:
      - channels:read
      - channels:history   # triggers the reduced rate limit outside the Marketplace
      - chat:write
settings:
  org_deploy_enabled: false
  socket_mode_enabled: false
  token_rotation_enabled: false   # cannot be disabled once enabled

# Drafted from the documented manifest structure. Validate with apps.manifest.validate before use.

handoffKit.title: Scope selection
handoffKit.content:
Post messages only: chat:write. No history access, so the reduced rate limits do not apply.
Read public channel history: channels:history and channels:read.
Read private channels, DMs or group DMs: groups:history, im:history, mpim:history. Request only those required; each must be justified in review.
Scope names are from Slack's API reference and were not re-verified in this research.

handoffKit.title: Draft scope justification for channels:history
handoffKit.content: <Product> is an assistant that summarises and answers questions about conversations in channels where a workspace member has added it. channels:history is required to read the messages the user asks the assistant to process. The app reads only channels it has been invited to, does not store message content beyond <retention period>, and does not use customer data to train models.

handoffKit.title: Connect the OAuth app to Composio
handoffKit.content:
1. In the Composio dashboard, open Auth Configs and create one for Slack using OAuth2 with your own developer credentials.
2. Enter the client ID and client secret. Set the redirect URI to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
3. Pass the auth config ID (ac_...) in your session's authConfigs, keyed by toolkit. Creating the auth config alone does not apply it.
Reference: https://docs.composio.dev/docs/authentication/custom-app-vs-managed-app
